script: Vermeer painted over a secret lover in this room. This is 'A Maid Asleep,' painted by Johannes Vermeer around 1657. At first glance, it's just a tired servant dozing off at a messy table. You've got a half-empty wine pitcher, some fruit, and this beautifully crumpled Turkish rug. But wait, look at the empty doorway on the right. When historians took an X-ray of this canvas, they found Vermeer had actually painted a man standing right there in the background, plus a dog in the doorway! By painting them out, Vermeer totally changed the vibe. Instead of an obvious romantic tryst, he gives us this deep, quiet mystery. Is she just exhausted from doing chores, or is she sleeping off too much wine, dreaming about someone who just slipped out the door? Vermeer was the absolute master of domestic drama, mostly because he knew exactly what to hide. By deleting the guy, he leaves the gossip entirely up to us. So, do you think she's sleeping off a hangover, or dreaming of a secret lover?
